title: Hark! a Voice Divides the Sky
description: Hark! a Voice Divides the Sky in Tonic Solfa to ST. BEES, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 548 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “"Blessed are the dead, that die in the Lord."”, where the book credits them to Wesley's Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. BEES; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Hark! a voice di-vides the sky! Hap-py are the faith-ful dead, In the Lord who sweet-ly die! They from all their toils are freed.

lines: Hark! a voice divides the sky!
In the Lord who sweetly die!
They from all their toils are freed.
Here they lay their burthen down,
Hallowed and made meet for heaven.
Yes! the Christian's course is run;
Fought the fight, the work is done;
Death is swallowed up in life.
When from flesh the spirit freed
